passage:
Counsellor's notes, employee wellbeing desk, 14 March
Noor, 24, came back for a second check-in. Last month she described nights of scrolling until 2 am and feeling flatter afterwards. This time she brought a page from her notebook.
Her plan: phone apps from 8:30 to 9:30 pm, then the phone charges in the kitchen. Each week, one offline thing: a Tuesday walk with a colleague from accounts, a Sunday call with her sister in Srinagar.
She said the first Tuesday walk felt awkward for ten minutes, then easy. 'I still use my phone,' she laughed. 'I just don't use it instead of people.'
She reports sleeping better, and the one walk has become two.
Next: follow-up in a month. I suggested adding a weekend plan only if she wants one.
- Hafsa

qa.q: Where does Noor's phone charge after 9:30 pm?
qa.a: The phone charges in the kitchen.

qa.q: What does Noor's laugh and line 'I just don't use it instead of people' suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Noor feels relieved and a little proud, having found a balance rather than giving up the phone altogether.

qa.q: Why does pairing a time window with an offline plan work better than the window alone?
qa.a: The window limits scrolling, while the walk and the call fill that time with real company, so the screen stays a tool rather than a replacement.

qa.q: What might Noor's sister in Srinagar get from the Sunday calls?
qa.a: Her sister likely gets a steady weekly connection and hears Noor's real voice, instead of only seeing posts.

grounding: It shows a young woman setting a window for phone use and pairing it with a weekly walk and call, keeping screens as a tool.

passage:
Wednesday, 10:05 pm
Day nine of The Rule: phone apps only between 7 and 8 at night, then airplane mode. I was sure I'd cheat by day three.
I did cheat once, on day four, watching a stranger renovate a flat in another country at midnight. Felt worse after, like always.
The second half of The Rule is the part that actually works: one real plan a week. Last Saturday I walked the lake loop with Aditi. We got lost behind the boat club and laughed so hard a dog barked at us. I didn't check my phone once and didn't miss it.
Tonight at 8 I put the phone down mid-reel. Zainab, you're getting good at this.
Called Aditi instead. We're doing the loop again on Saturday. Bringing better shoes.

qa.q: Where did Zainab and Aditi get lost?
qa.a: They got lost behind the boat club.

qa.q: How did Zainab feel after cheating at midnight on day four?
qa.a: Zainab felt low and regretful afterwards, the same bad feeling late scrolling always brought.

qa.q: Which half of The Rule does Zainab find more useful, and why?
qa.a: The one real plan a week, because the lake walk with Aditi gave laughter and company that scrolling never did.

qa.q: What might Aditi get out of the Saturday walks?
qa.a: Aditi gets a friend who is fully present rather than on a phone, which likely makes the walks fun enough to want to repeat.

grounding: It shows someone limiting phone time to a set hour and pairing it with a weekly walk with a friend, so screens stop replacing company.
